## LLM Recipe

### 1.3 Pretraining &amp; Optimization

#### [End-to-End 4-Bit Training](<https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/end-to-end-4-bit-training/>)

Thinking Machines describes a mixed-precision recipe that uses four-bit arithmetic for most expert-layer forward passes while retaining eight-bit backward computation. Re-quantizing saved forward tensors with stochastic rounding and compressing expert communications make low precision useful across pretraining and reinforcement learning. The authors report faster training on GB300 systems, alongside a small pretraining efficiency loss and limited public experimental detail.

**Published:** 2026-11-13 · **First seen:** 2026-11-14T11:01:01.560+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Mixed Precision, NVFP4, Stochastic Rounding, MoE

[Blog](<https://thinkingmachines.ai/blog/end-to-end-4-bit-training/>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small>)

**Evidence:** technical-report; full-text. Complete November 13 technical post inspected, including block-scaled transposes, stochastic re-quantization, communication formats and final recipe. Saved quantized forward weights/activations are dequantized, transposed and stochastically re-quantized to MXFP8 for backward GEMMs; 32-dimensional random Hadamard transforms and block-scaled S2F6 reduce combine payloads from 16 to 8.25 bits/value. Authors report 8% pretraining and 20% RL wall-clock speedups versus full MXFP8, with about 2% pretraining compute-efficiency loss. This is a delayed discovery within the 72-hour lookback: the post is dated November 13 and first retrieved today. Earlier Inkling 2 launch/card already disclosed native NVFP4 and the 68-hour run, but not these detailed numerical mechanisms; those older facts are not treated as new results.

**Limitations:** This is a GB300-specific author engineering report with in-house BBBK kernels, no controlled run table, seed intervals or independent reproduction. Four-bit applies to most expert forward computation, not the whole network or backward pass; the final one-sixth of layers uses MXFP8. Stochastic re-quantization targets the saved quantized forward value in expectation, not the original unquantized tensor or guaranteed unbiased total gradients. The 68-hour run combines many changes and does not isolate this recipe. Weights are public; a reproducible training/kernel implementation was not verified.

### 1.4 Mid-training &amp; Continual Learning

#### [daVinci-Prover: Agent-Native Mid-Training for Formal Theorem Proving](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16433>)

daVinci-Prover combines synthetic mathematical skill traces and verifier-grounded interactions in mid-training before supervised learning from successful Lean proving sessions. The added mid-training improves matched SFT-only baselines, supporting the value of learning an agent’s interaction patterns before downstream adaptation. The evidence concerns the tested theorem-proving benchmarks and substantial additional training, with broader capability retention and full artifact reproduction still unresolved.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.3 Context Engineering &amp; Memory

#### [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17316>)

CoReMem values a completed coding session by how much its contents help the next task on the inherited repository, then compresses useful experience into file locations and executable checks. It also adapts the coding agent to act on those memory anchors, making cross-task memory serve measured task resolution and effort rather than relevance alone. In the reported 27B ChainSWE comparison, the combined memory and training system raises resolution from 21.0% to 25.7% while reducing steps by 17% and session tokens by 11%, without measuring training cost or wall-clock savings.

### 2.6 Multi-Agent Collaboration

#### [Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16526>)

Lost in Delegation compares direct search with forced or optional delegation across four same-model agent families and factual queries from before and after their reported knowledge cutoffs. It shows how query rewriting and final-answer-only handoffs can lose evidence or error information, giving builders concrete failure modes to inspect before adding a coordinator. Delegation usually reduced accuracy in this protocol, but the result does not establish that heterogeneous teams, richer evidence sharing or interdependent tasks behave the same way.

### 3.3 Inference Engines &amp; Serving

#### [Cairn: Sharing and Prewarming Serverless LLM Startup Work](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16180>)

Cairn separates LLM startup into reusable model artifacts, model-independent setup that can run early, and process-bound CUDA graph capture, sharing the first group and replenishing prepared workers from a template process. On two emulated servers with RTX A6000 GPUs, this cuts cold starts by 4.1–5.2× for the tested 1B–14B models, offering a way to reduce serverless waiting beyond faster weight loading.

#### [Reducing Batch Makespan through Inference–Environment Coordination](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16661>)

This system jointly chooses hybrid-model cache allocation, trajectory-aware inference routing and scheduling, and separate limits for admitted tasks and executing environment jobs. Advancing long action chains helps finish batches sooner: the combined design reduces measured makespan by 10.4–65.0% across the tested Ling agent workloads, while the added chain scheduler contributes a smaller 3.1–8.5% on live MCP-Atlas runs.
